1.title: Closing a Project in Context
1.text: Welcome to Module sixteen: Closing a Project in Context. It covers the exam area The prince two processes. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. four point seven.one apply closing a project: activities, inputs and outputs, roles and responsibilities, how the practices are applied. four point seven.two analyze whether the activities, roles and responsibilities are effective and fit for purpose, considering tailoring, the practices, and the purpose and objectives of the process. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: The prince two processes (thirty percent). Exam format: an open-book scenario exam: one hundred fifty minutes, seventy marks, forty-two marks to pass. Validated against: the official prince two seven Practitioner syllabus (people cert), version seven point two.

1.title: Purpose, objectives and the principles it serves
1.text: Purpose, objectives and the principles it serves. Closing a project is the process that ends the project in an orderly way. It is the final stage of a planned project, or it is used early when the board stops the project. The figure shows the main flow.

1.title: Purpose, objectives and the principles it serves, continued
1.text: Purpose, objectives and the principles it serves. The figure shows this: Closing a project: confirm acceptance, hand over products, evaluate the project, recommend closure to the board and plan benefit reviews after the project.

1.title: Purpose, objectives and the principles it serves, continued
1.text: Purpose, objectives and the principles it serves. Purpose: provide a fixed point at which acceptance of the project product is confirmed, and recognize that the objectives in the P I D have been achieved, or that the project has nothing more to contribute. Objectives: acceptance is verified; products are handed to the people who will operate and support them; performance is reviewed against the baselines; benefits achieved so far are assessed and later benefit reviews are planned; follow-on actions are provided for; lessons are recorded.

1.title: Purpose, objectives and the principles it serves, continued
1.text: Purpose, objectives and the principles it serves. Continued business justification. Results are compared with the business case and benefits are followed up. Learn from experience. The lessons report goes to the corporate or programme level. Focus on products. Acceptance is checked against the acceptance criteria. Define roles, responsibilities and relationships. Ownership passes to operations and named owners. Manage by exception. A premature close follows a board decision. Exam tip: Acceptance first, then closure. The project manager recommends closure; the project board authorizes it.

1.title: Activities, inputs and outputs
1.text: Activities, inputs and outputs. The names below give the general idea; check the Official Book's wording for the activities. Prepare planned closure. Checks that all work is done and approved against the project product description; closes or passes on open issues and risks. Prepare premature closure. After the board decides to stop early, records what was done and not done, and salvages the products. Hand over products. Passes products to those who will operate them; confirms acceptance and that support is in place.

1.title: Activities, inputs and outputs, continued
1.text: Activities, inputs and outputs. Evaluate the project. Reviews performance against the P I D baselines; writes the end project report and lessons report; plans benefit reviews. Recommend project closure. Sends the board the closure recommendation; prepares to release resources and archive records.

1.title: Activities, inputs and outputs, continued
1.text: Activities, inputs and outputs. Inputs. Project product description and acceptance criteria; product approvals; P I D baselines; project log; benefits management approach; the board's instruction for a premature close. Outputs. End project report; lessons report; follow-on action recommendations; benefits review plan; acceptance and handover records; closure recommendation; archived records. Follow-on actions and the benefits review plan travel with the end project report and the benefits management approach. Check the book for where each is held. Exam tip: Benefits are reviewed after the project, so closing needs a benefits review plan with an owner. Keeping a project open to measure benefits is a red flag.

1.title: Roles
1.text: Roles. Project manager. Responsible: plans and carries out closure, hands over, writes the reports, recommends closure. Project board. Receives the recommendation and authorizes closure, in directing a project. Executive. Confirms the objectives were met; makes sure benefit reviews have an owner. Senior user. Confirms the products meet user needs and are accepted for use.

1.title: Roles, continued
1.text: Roles. Senior supplier. Confirms supplier work is complete and supports the handover. Team manager. Hands over delivered products and their records. Project assurance. Checks independently that acceptance is real and the reports are fair. Project support. Archives records, closes the logs, helps prepare the reports. Check the book's roles table. Lessons and follow-on actions go to the corporate or programme level, which also tracks benefits.

1.title: How the practices are applied
1.text: How the practices are applied. Business case. Compare results with the business case; plan benefit reviews. Organization. Hand over to operations; release the team and suppliers. Plans. Compare actuals with the baselined plans. Quality. Confirm every product meets its acceptance criteria. Risk. Pass residual risks on to named owners. Issues. Close open issues or pass them on as follow-on actions. Progress. End project report, lessons report, and final update of the logs.

1.title: Judging a scenario
1.text: Judging a scenario. Acceptance confirmed against the criteria by the right people. Closure recommended before acceptance, or acceptance assumed. Products handed to operations with training and support. Operations left unready, so the service fails. End project report compares results with the P I D baselines. A report that only lists activities. Benefits reviewed after the project, with an owner, dates and measures. Benefit tracking ends when the team disbands.

1.title: Judging a scenario, continued
1.text: Judging a scenario. Follow-on actions, open issues and risks passed to named owners. Unfinished work disappears or is called phase two with no record. Lessons sent to the corporate or programme level. Lessons stay in the project manager's head. Premature close: the board decides, the project manager salvages, hands over and records. The project is abandoned, or the project manager stops it alone.

2.title: Judging a scenario, continued
2.text: Judging a scenario. Tailoring changes the size of the closure, not the confirmation of acceptance. Small projects: a short end project report, lessons in the log and one acceptance and handover meeting. Agile or incremental delivery: earlier releases are already accepted; closing confirms the final state, and unfinished backlog items become follow-on actions. Supplier projects: confirm each contract is complete under the commercial management approach, and release suppliers. Sustainability, digital and data: retire the old process safely, archive or dispose of data by the rules, and add sustainability measures to the benefit reviews. Exam tip: A premature close still uses closing a project: salvage, hand over, record, learn. The board decides to stop, and the project manager does not simply walk away.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. At the end of Project Harbor's rollout stage, Sam Okafor sends the board an end project report and recommends closure. Tomas Reyes, the senior user, has not yet confirmed that the permit service meets the acceptance criteria. Was this an appropriate action for the project manager to take, and why? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: No, because acceptance must come before a recommendation to close. Closing a project is the fixed point at which acceptance is confirmed, so it comes before the recommendation, and the board then authorizes closure.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. Project Harbor's permit service is live and accepted. The port's operations team has had no training and has no support guide. What should Sam do before recommending closure? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Arrange a handover with training and support information. Handing products over so that operations can support them is part of closing a project, and benefits are reviewed after the project.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. The port's board cancels Project Harbor after the build stage because permits will be outsourced. Sam salvages the finished products, hands them to the port's I T team, records what was not done and why, writes the lessons and recommends closure. Was this an appropriate action, and why? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Yes, because a premature close still hands over and records lessons. A premature close uses closing a project to salvage value, hand over, record and learn, with the board's authority.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. Project Harbor's permit service is complete. Who should confirm that it meets the users' needs and acceptance criteria? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Tomas Reyes, the senior user. The senior user speaks for the users and confirms that the products meet their needs, while project assurance only checks independently.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. Sam must give the board a review of how Project Harbor performed against the budget, time, quality and benefits baselined in the P I D. Which management product provides this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: End project report. The end project report reviews the whole project against its baselines at closure.

2.title: Practice Question 6
2.text: Question six. Sam proposes to close Project Harbor once the service is accepted and handed over, with a benefits review six months later and a named owner. Was this an appropriate approach, and why? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Yes, because benefits appear after the project, so an owner reviews them. Many benefits only appear after the project, so a benefits review plan with an owner continues the follow-up.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What is the purpose of closing a project? Answer: To provide a fixed point at which acceptance of the project product is confirmed and the P I D objectives are recognized as achieved. Question two. Name the five activities. Answer: Prepare planned closure, prepare premature closure, hand over products, evaluate the project and recommend project closure. Question three. Which two reports does the project manager write to evaluate the project? Answer: The end project report and the lessons report.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Who authorizes project closure? Answer: The project board, on the project manager's recommendation. Question five. What is a premature close? Answer: Closing the project early because the board decides to stop it. Question six. Why are benefits reviewed after the project? Answer: Many benefits only appear after the project has ended.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Purpose: confirm acceptance and that the P I D objectives are achieved. Activities: planned closure, premature closure, hand over, evaluate, recommend closure. Outputs: end project report, lessons report, follow-on actions, benefits review plan. Decision: the project manager recommends; the board authorizes. Effective: acceptance, handover, honest report, benefit reviews with an owner. Red flags: no acceptance, unready operations, benefits dropped, abandoned project. Premature close: board stops; salvage, hand over, record, learn. Tailoring: smaller closure, never skipping acceptance.
